result:
Both defects are fixed, each in its own local commit with a test. Neither is pushed; the driver runs the full suite and pushes.

- **#1202, `bdf3e2ff`** (`Fixes #1202`): the checker gave an `ident` (or `intern(p)`) binding no type. So an action handing it to a rule returning `winnow_grammar::Symbol?` was never wrapped in `Some`, and rustc refused it. `reference_type` in `check_grammar.nika` now types both as `winnow_grammar::Symbol`, and the existing wrapping does the rest.
- **#1203, `fed74cdc`** (`Fixes #1203`): the cause is narrower than the issue says. The text-tier pass in `text_tiers.nika` walked a loop body only once, top to bottom. So `return previous`, written above `previous = line.trim()`, still saw only the `""` literal, and the result became `&'static str`. Returning `previous` after the loop already worked. A new `tier_loop_turns` walks a `for` or `while` body again until nothing it tracks for the outer variables changes. Each walk only adds to what is known, so it stops. The probe now lowers as `fn before<'r>(text: &'r str, name: &'r str) -> &'r str` and runs.

Tests:
- Both new `tests/compiler` programs fail on the old binary and pass on the new one.
- The whole `tests/compiler` project passes, 600 of 600 in both settings. In the full run, 6 tests first failed because `target/fast/nikaia` disappeared mid-run (another agent rebuilding), and `agent_script` hit a missing temp file. All 7 passed when run alone.
- The `it` grammar, text-tier and view modules pass (203 tests). Clippy, `cargo fmt`, `pre-push` and the `lower-std` fixpoint are clean.
- I did not run the corpus guard that is already red on develop (figure 18).

Disk: the test cache is 1.1G and 5.3G is free. Entries over 100 MB new in this run: build-time-parsers 523 MB, run-bundle 211 MB, rlib 199 MB.

Nothing is open, and I found no errors in other agents' files.
